A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Graph Fourier Neural ODE research. All pages, including v2's Appendices A–C, are readable, and the text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison. V1 has no appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original MD17 prediction experiments, component ablations, long-horizon evaluations and a Benzene spectral case study.

after.justification: V2 reports original MD17 and alanine dipeptide experiments, including structural measurements, temporal super-resolution and additional ablations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The GFT–ODE–inverse-GFT pipeline remains, but v2 introduces attention between previously independently propagated frequency modes and separates scalar and vector ODE dynamics. It also introduces vector-feature centering and restoration and replaces the EGNN-only architecture with alternative GNN backbones, explicitly evaluated in Table 9. These change the reported procedure beyond expanded documentation.

E1.justification: V2 retains all eight MD17 molecules and adds alanine dipeptide conformational prediction, extending coverage to a peptide system. It also evaluates a distinct temporal super-resolution task requiring predictions at ten times the training resolution.

E2.justification: LG-ODE is newly evaluated in the MD17 comparison in Table 1 and in additional comparisons, including Figure 6. NDCN, EGNN, EGNO and ITO remain in the main MD17 table. The reported long-horizon comparison drops NDCN between v1 Figure 2 and v2 Figure 7.

E3.justification: V2 adds regular-timestep training and evaluation in Appendix B, tenfold temporal-resolution testing, and structural MAE, relative-error and TICA evaluation criteria. The existing 500/2000/2000 sample split and 3000-step horizon remain unchanged. Sampling eight frames per instance is newly disclosed, rather than an established change to the earlier experiment.

E4.justification: V2 expands the two original component ablations into scalar/vector ODE, GFT-versus-FFT, mode-interaction, mode-count, backbone and time-embedding studies, including alanine ablations. It adds structural-recovery and TICA analyses. The long-horizon study remains, but v1's Benzene case study relating spatial modes to temporal Fourier spectra is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report numerical results with ± uncertainty and use graphical uncertainty indicators. Neither specifies repeated-run counts, seeds or the estimator underlying those uncertainties. V2 extends the existing reporting practice without introducing a stated statistical estimation or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: V1's entire Table 1 'Ours' row reappears as EGNNConv in v2 Table 9. V2's headline row reports different configurations and values, including Benzene 1.52 versus the earlier 40.86 on the MD17 table's ×10−2 scale; this is not an isolated same-model gain. V2 also adds alanine MSE results, structural errors, regular-sampling results, super-resolution findings and numerous ablation results.

T1.justification: V2 adds a spectral-truncation theorem, bandlimited recovery claims, proofs and an error-control corollary in Section 3.3 and Appendix C; v1 supplies only basic transform and model equations. The additions contain errors: λM−1 ≤ α alone does not ensure retention of every supported mode, and Corollary C.6's stated assumptions imply a √ε norm bound, not ε.

C1.justification: The central novelty and accuracy claims remain joint spatial-spectral and continuous-time molecular modeling. V2 adds headline claims about preserving molecular geometry and successful temporal super-resolution, extending the advertised capabilities while retaining the central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 introduces a Benzene-drift explanation for backbone performance and uses it to motivate standard message passing over EGNN layers. It adds interpretations concerning structural recovery, slow-mode alignment and diminishing returns from additional Fourier modes. V1's spectrum-based interpretation, including its qualification that spatial and temporal frequencies lack strict one-to-one correspondence, is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a stated public implementation link and extensive reproducibility information in Appendix A: optimizer, learning rate, weight decay, epochs, batch size, hidden dimension, eight-frame sampling, solver tolerances and checkpoint selection. It also documents simulation time units and molecule-specific retained-mode counts. These are largely new disclosures, not evidence that previously unspecified settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 replaces the spectroscopy-led motivation with more extensive positioning against Fourier neural operators and graph neural ODEs. Related work broadens from coarse-grained MD to classical force-field and ab initio simulation, adds several FNO and ODE references, and introduces spectral-graph and TICA foundations. Several earlier spectroscopy and coarse-graining references disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Separate problem-definition, preliminaries and method sections become an integrated proposed-approach section; experimental questions and subsections are reorganized. V2 also separates the conclusion and broader-impact statement, introduces appendices and consistently names the framework GF-NODE.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the original combined spectroscopy/architecture figure with redesigned framework and scale illustrations, redraws the long-horizon plots and removes the Benzene spectral figure. It adds molecular snapshots, TICA, super-resolution and mode-count plots. The original combined comparison/ablation table becomes separate displays, accompanied by numerous new main-text and appendix tables and a changed document layout.

improvement.justification: The added alanine, regular-sampling, structural and component evaluations strengthen empirical support, while Appendix A substantially improves reproducibility information. However, the new theoretical justification contains incorrect recovery and error-bound claims in Theorem 3.2 and Corollary C.6, and the direct spatial/temporal-spectrum case study is lost. These weaknesses limit the net quality gain despite the broader evidence and clearer implementation disclosure.
